- p0: Value of the positive case in the raw data (e.g., "Pass")
- p1: Display value for the positive case (e.g., "OK")
- n1: Display value for the negative case (e.g., "NG")

Values that match p0 are transformed to p1;
all other values are transformed to n1 for display.
If no positive case exists (e.g., defect history data), set p0 to Null.

Waveform Plot Description:
You can visualize waveforms for each cycle.
Multiple waveforms can be plotted on a single graph, and coloring is also supported.
For example, by comparing press‑fit waveforms, current waveforms,
or vibration waveforms of good and defective products,
you can identify rising‑edge changes in specific sections or detect variations in peak positions.

Selecting a 'Div' variable (used to group identical waveforms, such as Cycle ID) is mandatory.

Layout hover messenger:
After selecting the primary variable(s), specify the additional data to display.

Common settings (applied to all primary variables)
   X-axis (optional): Select the variable to use for the X-axis. If omitted, data order is used.
   Lab: Specify the label displayed in the plot.
   LabX: Display labels using the X-axis values.
   Color: Color-code data by the variable's category values.
   ColorX: Color-code data by the X-axis category values.
   ColImb: Display categories with extremely small values on a secondary axis.
   ColImbX: Color-code the categories displayed on the secondary axis.
       - Only the top 16 categories by data count are displayed. Categories with the same count are ordered by date/time.
       - When Color (Imb) is selected, settings cannot be configured individually for each primary variable.

Settings for each primary variable
 Specify the data to add or split for each primary variable.
(The numeric prefix indicates the order in which the primary variables were selected.)
   1-Lab: Specify the label to display for this primary variable.
   1-Step: Specify a step variable (used to display thresholds or control values).

Overlay multiple variables
   1-Main: Add a variable to the primary (left) axis.
   1-2nd: Add a variable to the secondary (right) axis (up to 3 variables).
   1-Auto: Overlay a variable without assigning it to an axis.
       - Up to 8 variables can be specified per primary variable (1-Main + 1-2nd + 1-Auto + 1-Step).

Split by category values
   1Color: Color-code data by the variable's category values.
   1ColImb: Display categories with extremely small values on a secondary axis.
       - Up to 8 category values are displayed (only the top 8 categories by data count).
